answer.sameness: Two template families dominate. (1) Originals: a full-bleed photo hero with a white or dark card overlapping it bottom-left, serif headline (gostilna-pri-mostu, zlata-zlica, na-gricu, pizzeria-oljka, trgovina-oljka-in-sol, cvetlicarna) or a dark photo hero with heavy condensed sans in caps and a fake licence-plate phone number plus blue/yellow strip (avto-kovac, avtoservis-mrak, karoserija-hribar, vulkanizer-zorman, kljucavnicarstvo). (2) Regenerated: a near-identical split layout, text left on white/light grey, one rectangular photo right, same small 'Pokličite / Navodila za pot' pill pair in the header, same contact block (phone, address, hours) in three columns. Giant pale script word be…
recurringIssues: Regenerated versions collapse into one anonymous white split layout; business identity is lost and empty right-hand areas appear (prevajanje, racunovodstvo, vulkanizer regenerated).
Hero text cut off at the fold or sections starting mid-way with orphaned headings ('Kdaj sem odprta', 'Cene inštrukcij', 'Delamo od leta' with half-cropped '2004').
Phone versions stack hero photo under long text so many first screens are text-only or show photos chopped at the bottom.
Identical hair-salon imagery (same blonde balayage photo) across Lana and Tina; same house-under-tree photo across Zlata Žlica and Na Griču.
Low-contrast small body text on dark photo heros (kmetija-grabnar, gostisce, vulkanizer); readability on phone weak.
Decorative details (zigzag strips, licence plates, giant script words) are repeated across unrelated trades, so they read as studio tics not brand ideas.
Photos are generic stock crops (keys, copper pipes, plug illustration) with little relation to the actual business.

best.why: Dark warm palette, strong bread photo, price badge and good serif headline give a real bakery mood with clear hierarchy on both desktop and phone.
Burgundy split hero with atmospheric shaving-brush photo feels specifically like a barbershop rather than a template.
Full-bleed mountain photo with location pills and a serif headline gives place and hospitality; the mobile version holds together.

weakest.why: Bare white text block with no imagery, a stray heading floating below, and no visual sense of a tyre shop.
Dense grey text and contact list, no image or colour, hierarchy flat; reads as an unfinished document.
Empty right half, headline then void; the only visual is a giant cropped year further down.

answer.oneChange: Stop regenerating into the one white split-hero template; give each trade a committed art direction (palette, type pairing, one signature photo treatment) and make the first phone screen show headline, image and one action without cropping.
answer.summary: As a portfolio this reads as two templates: a photo-with-overlapping-card look and a text-left/photo-right white look, with a condensed-caps 'garage' variant for car trades. A few pages (pekarna-kvas, brivnica-kos-regenerated, kmetija-grabnar) show real character; most regenerated pages drain it out, leaving white space, repeated header pills and stock crops. Recurring faults: headings cut at the fold, duplicated photos between clients, weak contrast on dark heroes, and phone screens that are mostly text. Competent and tidy, but a client could mistake half of these sites for each other. Commit to distinct art direction per business and fix the fold and mobile composition before adding more pages.
